title: Kunti
hook: before the war, Kunti gives Krishna a message for her sons, and the message is a story about another mother who would not let her son lie down

segments.voice: Yesterday, Kunti at Ekachakra, offering one of her own sons to repay the family who sheltered them.

Krishna's peace mission has failed. Before he leaves Hastinapura, he goes to see his aunt, who has stayed behind in the city while her sons waited out their exile. He asks if she has a message for them. She does, but she doesn't start with advice. She starts with a story, an old one, she says, about a woman named Vidula and her son. Kunti wants her sons to hear it before the war. Today, at the end of a week of the epics' women, Kunti speaks through someone else's voice.
screen: `THE PEACE MISSION HAS FAILED.` → `A MESSAGE FOR HER SONS.` → `SHE TELLS THEM A STORY.`

segments.voice: The story is in the Mahabharata's Book of Effort, here in paraphrase. Vidula is a proud woman of a warrior family. Her son Sanjaya has been beaten by a rival king, and now he lies at home, low and listless. Vidula goes to him, and she is not gentle. Get up, she tells him. You were not born to lie here. Then this line, which in Sanskrit runs muhurtam jvalitam shreyo, na tu dhumayitam ciram: better to blaze up for a moment than to smolder for a long time. Her son argues back. What good will a kingdom be to you, he asks, if I'm dead? She answers him again and again until he rises. Then Kunti adds her own words to Krishna, for Arjuna and Bhima: the time has come for which a mother of warriors bears sons. Kunti, who asked Krishna for trouble in the Bhagavata, here asks her sons to walk toward it. She doesn't only command; she tells a story and lets it work. It's not a comfortable passage. Some readers hear courage; others hear the cost of a war a mother has just urged. The epic keeps both. And it closes a week of women: Sita, answering Rama before the army; Draupadi, keeping accounts, waiting by an empty pot, asking for a killer's life; and Kunti, who sends a story ahead of her sons.
screen: `VIDULA AND HER BEATEN SON` · `BLAZE A MOMENT, DON'T SMOLDER` · `KUNTI SPEAKS THROUGH THE STORY` · `A WEEK OF THE EPICS' WOMEN`

segments.voice: Ask gently whether one thing in your life has been smoldering a long time, a call or a task you keep not starting, and don't scold yourself: Vidula's words were for a warrior, and yours can be kinder. Let it come into view, warmth gathering around it like an ember on each breath in, one first step appearing on each breath out. If you pray, you can ask for courage. And if low days ever start to feel like there's no point, please reach out: in the US, call or text 988, or your local emergency number.
Kunti. Before the war, she sent her sons the story of Vidula: better to blaze for a moment than to smolder for a long time. Today's word.
Your line: Kunti. Better to blaze a moment than to smolder long. That's a week of the epics' women.

howItsDone: Hindus meet Kunti's message and the story of Vidula in fuller retellings and commentaries on the Mahabharata's Udyoga Parva, where it is read as a lesson about courage and duty.
